rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both orders delegate presidential authority to approve regulations without further presidential action and then expressly extend that delegation to later alteration or termination of those regulations. This combination, including closely matched phrasing and the same two-stage administrative machinery, is materially more distinctive than a generic delegation clause. C05 has a similar express expansion of delegated authority, while C04 combines delegation to the Budget Director with regulation-supersession machinery, but neither matches the child's core structure as closely as C01.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Director of the Bureau of the Budget is hereby authorized and empowered, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, to exercise the authority vested in the President ... to approve regulations prescribed pursuant to that section
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Postmaster General is hereby designated and empowered to exercise without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President the authority vested in the President ... to approve regulations issued by the Secretary of the Treasury
shared_material.explanation: The operative delegation formula and the specifically delegated function—presidential approval of another official's regulations—are nearly identical.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The authority delegated ... shall be deemed to include the authority to approve the amendment, supersede, or termination of regulations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: and to approve any amendment or repeal of any of such regulations by the Secretary of the Treasury
shared_material.explanation: Both expressly make the delegated approval power cover subsequent amendment or termination of the regulations, creating substantially the same administrative machinery.
